By the end of the hour there's a tiny silver bell-flower that rings when you breathe on it.|You plant the warm one. It comes up in minutes, a fern that curls round your finger like a cat's tail.|You plant it and it grows into something nobody in the club can name. You get to name it. You choose well.} {It sprouts at once, straight up your nose. You sneeze pollen for the rest of the day.|It grows a single angry thorn and nothing else, and the thorn finds your thumb.|It's a nettle that stings in rhymes. You'll be hearing them in your sleep.} Sort the tin properly {You sort the packets by family, season and handwriting. The club will never know it was you, which is the nice part.|You sort the lot and label the unlabelled ones. "SORRY" turns out to be turnips, which explains a great deal.|You file the picture-packets by guessing from the drawings. You're right about most of them, you think.}
